sylphx.notify.v1.MailServer.description: One mail server of a connected mailbox.

port.description: The port; IMAP 993 and SMTP 465 when unset.

username.description: The login user; the mailbox address when unset.

sylphx.notify.v1.MailServerSecurity.description: How a mail server connection is secured.

sylphx.notify.v1.Mailbox.description:
A Mailbox is an email address Notify reads from and sends as. A `CONNECTED`
mailbox is an existing mailbox at any provider, reached over IMAP (read
only) and SMTP with its own login, either a password or an OAuth 2.0 grant
(XOAUTH2) at Google or Microsoft; a `HOSTED` mailbox receives at an
address whose MX is Sylphx. Mail it receives becomes Inbound Email records.

name.description: `orgs/{org}/projects/{project}/envs/{env}/mailboxes/{mailbox}`.

sylphx.notify.v1.MailboxAuthKind.description: How a connected Mailbox logs in.

sylphx.notify.v1.MailboxConnectLink.description:
A Mailbox Connect Link is a hosted page that a platform customer's server
mints with its own server key for one end user, who approves the
provider's consent there. The mailbox it connects lives in the customer's
environment, and the end user signs in to nothing of Sylphx and sees no
Sylphx name. It is single use and expires (the Stripe Account Link model):
pressing Continue on the page claims it, so a link preview's fetch does
not; a claimed or expired link sends the end user to `refresh_url`, where
the customer's server mints a new one.

backfill_start_time.description:
The new mailbox reads mail received on or after this day on its first
poll.

complete_time.description: When the end user finished, connected or failed.

connected_mailbox.description: The mailbox it connected or reconnected.

display_name.description: The From display name of the new mailbox.

error_code.description:
Why it failed: `consent_denied`, `scope_missing` (the end user unticked a
scope), `address_mismatch` (a reconnect signed in as another address),
`address_in_use` (another mailbox of the environment has the address),
`plan_limit_reached`, or `provider_error`.

expire_time.description: When it expires.

login_hint.description:
The address to suggest on the consent screen (`login_hint`); the
mailbox takes the address the provider confirms, whatever this says.

mailbox.description:
The mailbox to reconnect, keeping its id and feed; it must be signed in
as the same address. Empty creates a new connected mailbox.

mailbox_id.description: The id of the new mailbox; the server assigns one when empty.

meta.description: Resource metadata; labels may carry the customer's own end-user id.

name.description: `orgs/{org}/projects/{project}/envs/{env}/mailbox_connect_links/{mailbox_connect_link}`.

provider.description:
The provider whose consent the page opens; the environment needs that
provider's Mailbox OAuth App.

refresh_url.description:
Where a claimed or expired link sends the end user, HTTPS; your server
mints a new link there. Empty shows a page saying the link has expired.

return_url.description:
Where the end user lands when done, HTTPS, with `connect_link={id}` and
`result=connected` or `result=failed` added to the query. The query
proves nothing: read the link back with your key for the outcome.

ttl.description: How long the link stays open; default 1 hour, at most 7 days.

url.description:
The link to hand the end user. It is a bearer secret: only the create
call returns it, and only its hash is stored.

sylphx.notify.v1.MailboxConnectLinkState.description: The lifecycle of a Mailbox Connect Link.

sylphx.notify.v1.MailboxOauthApp.description:
A Mailbox OAuth App is the platform customer's own OAuth client at Google
or Microsoft. End users consent to it, so the consent screen names the
customer's app and never Sylphx, and every `OAUTH` mailbox of its provider
in the environment refreshes its grant against it. An environment has at
most one per provider.

name.description: `orgs/{org}/projects/{project}/envs/{env}/mailbox_oauth_apps/{mailbox_oauth_app}`.

sylphx.notify.v1.MailboxOauthAppSpec.description: MailboxOauthAppSpec is the caller-writable state of a Mailbox OAuth App.

client_id.description: The client id the provider issued.

client_secret.description: The client secret; write-only, sealed at rest, never returned.

tenant.description:
Microsoft only: who may consent, `common` (the default: any work, school
or personal account), `organizations`, `consumers`, or one tenant id.

sylphx.notify.v1.MailboxOauthAppStatus.description: MailboxOauthAppStatus is the observed state of a Mailbox OAuth App.

client_secret_set.description: Whether a client secret is stored.

observed_generation.description: The generation this status was computed from.

redirect_uri.description: The redirect URI to register on the provider's client.

scopes.description:
The scopes a connect link asks for: Google `https://mail.google.com/`
(a restricted scope: a public app needs Google's verification), and
Microsoft `IMAP.AccessAsUser.All`, `SMTP.Send` and `offline_access`, each
with `openid email` to learn the address.

sylphx.notify.v1.MailboxOauthProvider.description: An OAuth provider of connected mailboxes.

sylphx.notify.v1.MailboxSpec.description: MailboxSpec is the caller-writable state of a Mailbox.

append_sent.description:
Save a copy of mail sent as this mailbox to its Sent folder (IMAP
APPEND); off when the provider saves one itself.

auth_kind.description: How a connected mailbox logs in to both servers; unset means `PASSWORD`.

backfill_start_time.description: Read mail received on or after this day on the first poll.

display_name.description: The From display name of mail sent as this mailbox.

enabled.description: Poll and send; a disabled mailbox keeps its records.

oauth_provider.description:
The OAuth provider, for `OAUTH`; the environment's Mailbox OAuth App of
this provider is the client the grant belongs to. With `imap` or `smtp`
unset the provider's own servers are used: Google `imap.gmail.com:993`
and `smtp.gmail.com:465`, Microsoft `outlook.office365.com:993` and
`smtp.office365.com:587` (STARTTLS).

oauth_refresh_token.description:
The OAuth refresh token, for `OAUTH`; write-only, sealed at rest like the
password, never returned. A connect link sets it without the caller ever
holding it; a caller that ran its own consent may set it directly, when
the token was issued to the environment's Mailbox OAuth App.

password.description: The login password of both servers; write-only, sealed at rest.

smtp.description: SMTP submission, for a connected mailbox.

sylphx.notify.v1.MailboxStatus.description: MailboxStatus is the observed state of a Mailbox.

last_error.description: The last poll's error; empty after a clean poll.

last_poll_time.description: When the mailbox was last read.

oauth_refresh_token_set.description: Whether an OAuth refresh token is stored.

observed_generation.description: The generation this status was computed from.

reconnect_required.description:
The provider refused the refresh token (revoked, expired, or the
account's password changed): the mailbox neither polls nor sends until a
connect link naming it, or a new `oauth_refresh_token`, reconnects it.

sent_folder.description: The Sent folder found on the server.

name.description: The name of the inbox item.
The name of the inbox item.

sylphx.notify.v1.Message.description:
A Message is one notification to one recipient on one topic. Notify admits
it idempotently, checks suppression and preferences, and fans it out to the
allowed channels with fallback and digesting; every delivery closes with a
provider receipt that only Notify writes.

broadcast.description: The broadcast that created it, if any.

capture.description: A test recipient's rendered content; empty for every other recipient.

channels.description:
Restrict to these channels, in fallback order; empty uses the recipient's
preferences.

content.description:
Inline content, only with `mailbox`: the subject and bodies as written,
not rendered from a template.

data.description: Template variables.

delivery_deadline_time.description:
Deliver no later than this; a delivery still open then fails with
`expired`. Unset retries for up to a day. The message record is kept.

email_message_id.description: The Message-ID Notify gave the email, without angle brackets.

mailbox.description:
Send as this mailbox (its address, display name and, for a connected
mailbox, its own SMTP) instead of a verified Email Domain.

name.description: `orgs/{org}/projects/{project}/envs/{env}/messages/{message}`.

parent_message_id.description: In-Reply-To: the Message-ID this answers, without angle brackets.

references.description: The thread's Message-IDs, oldest first, without angle brackets.

state_reason.description:
Why the message is in its state, for example `recipient_interval` for
`RATE_LIMITED` or `suppressed` for `SUPPRESSED`.

template.description: The template to render; required unless `mailbox` and `content` are set.

template_version.description: The template version rendered; pinned at admission.

topic.description: The topic preferences are checked against, for example `billing`.

sylphx.notify.v1.MessageCapture.description: What a message to a test recipient rendered to.

links.description: Every link in the bodies, in order.

sylphx.notify.v1.MessageContent.description: Inline content of a Message sent as a mailbox.

sylphx.notify.v1.Preference.description:
A Preference is a recipient's choice for one topic: which channels may carry
it. Admission honors it, and unsubscribe links write it. The id is the
topic.

channels.description: Channels the topic may use; empty mutes the topic.

digest_interval.description:
Batch this topic into a digest at most this often; unset sends each
message.

name.description: `orgs/{org}/projects/{project}/envs/{env}/recipients/{recipient}/preferences/{preference}`.

data.description: Data delivered with the notification.

sylphx.notify.v1.PushDevice.description: A push device of a recipient.

sender.description: The push Sender the token belongs to.

token_last4.description: The last four characters of the token, for display.

app_key.description: The bundle id, package name, or web origin.

connection.description: The Connection holding the APNs, FCM, or VAPID credentials.

sylphx.notify.v1.Recipient.description:
A Recipient is one of a customer's users, across channels: email addresses,
phone numbers, and device tokens. Dead device tokens are pruned from
provider feedback.

external_key.description: The customer's own id for this user, for example an Auth end user name.

language_code.description: BCP 47 language for templates; default the environment's.

name.description: `orgs/{org}/projects/{project}/envs/{env}/recipients/{recipient}`.

phone_numbers.description: E.164 phone numbers, first is preferred.

test.description:
A test recipient: its messages are rendered and captured on the Message,
never delivered. An email address whose local part carries
`+sylphx_test` is a test address whatever this says.

time_zone.description: IANA time zone for quiet hours and digests.

sylphx.notify.v1.Route.description:
A Route sends the mail a receiving Email Domain accepts for one address, a
pattern of addresses, or every other address to actions: deliver to
mailboxes, forward, or reject. Every accepted message also publishes
`sylphx.notify.inbound_email.received`.

name.description: `orgs/{org}/projects/{project}/envs/{env}/mail_domains/{mail_domain}/mail_routes/{mail_route}`.

sylphx.notify.v1.RouteAction.description: One thing a Route does with mail; exactly one.

mailbox.description: Deliver to a mailbox of the environment.

reject.description: Refuse at the recipient step with this message; stands alone.

sylphx.notify.v1.RouteMatch.description: Which recipients a Route matches; exactly one.

address.description:
A local part, for example `support`. A local part with a `+tag` also
matches its route.

catch_all.description: Every local part no other route matches.

pattern.description: A glob on the local part, for example `billing-*`.

sylphx.notify.v1.RouteSpamPolicy.description: What happens to mail judged spam on a Route.

sylphx.notify.v1.RouteSpec.description: RouteSpec is the caller-writable state of a Route.

actions.description:
What happens to the mail: one or more mailbox and forward actions, or one
reject.

spam.description: What happens to mail the spam filter judges spam; `DELIVER` when unset.

sylphx.notify.v1.RouteStatus.description: RouteStatus is the observed state of a Route.

observed_generation.description: The generation this status was computed from.

etag.description: Act only if the current etag matches.

name.description: The name of the broadcast.

validate_only.description: Validate without writing anything.

sylphx.notify.v1.SendLimit.description:
A per-recipient send limit. A message over it is recorded with state
`RATE_LIMITED` and its create answers 429 `RATE_LIMITED` with the wait.

max_per_hour.description: At most this many messages to one recipient in any hour; 0 is no limit.

min_interval.description: At least this long between two messages to one recipient.

sylphx.notify.v1.Sender.description:
A Sender is a verified origin for SMS or push: a registered number or sender
id, or a push app whose APNs/FCM credentials are a Connection reached
through the credential service. It is used only once verified.

name.description: `orgs/{org}/projects/{project}/envs/{env}/senders/{sender}`.

sylphx.notify.v1.SenderSpec.description: SenderSpec is the caller-writable state of a Sender.

push.description: A mobile or web push app.

sms.description: An SMS number or alphanumeric sender id.

sylphx.notify.v1.SenderStatus.description: SenderStatus is the observed state of a Sender.

observed_generation.description: The generation this status was computed from.

verification_note.description: Why the sender is not verified, when it is not.

verified.description: Whether the sender is registered and usable.

region_codes.description: CLDR region codes the origin is registered for.

sender_key.description: An alphanumeric sender id, where the region allows one.

sylphx.notify.v1.Suppression.description:
A Suppression stops delivery to one address on one channel. Bounces,
complaints, carrier opt-outs, uninstalled devices, and unsubscribes write
it; admission checks it before accepting a message.

address.description: The suppressed address, number, or device token.

name.description: `orgs/{org}/projects/{project}/envs/{env}/suppressions/{suppression}`.

reason.description: Why.

source_message.description: The message whose feedback wrote it.

topic.description: Limit the suppression to one topic; unset suppresses every topic.

sylphx.notify.v1.Template.description:
A Template is versioned content per channel. Every spec change is a new
version; a message renders from the version it pinned at admission.

name.description: `orgs/{org}/projects/{project}/envs/{env}/templates/{template}`.

sylphx.notify.v1.TemplateSpec.description: TemplateSpec is the caller-writable state of a Template.

send_limit.description:
A per-recipient send limit on messages rendered from this template;
unset admits every message.

sylphx.notify.v1.TemplateStatus.description: TemplateStatus is the observed state of a Template.

observed_generation.description: The generation this status was computed from.

version.description: The version the current spec is; messages pin it.

sylphx.observability.v1.ErrorEvent.description:
An Error Event is one immutable error occurrence, with breadcrumbs and
correlation.

breadcrumbs.description: Breadcrumbs before the error, oldest first, at most 100.

name.description: `orgs/{org}/projects/{project}/envs/{env}/error_groups/{error_group}/error_events/{error_event}`.

stack.description:
The stack as the runtime printed it (JavaScript `Error.stack`), at most
64 KiB. When `stack_frames` is empty, V8 (`at fn (file:line:col)`) and
Gecko/WebKit (`fn@file:line:col`) lines are parsed into `stack_frames`,
innermost last; when `stack_frames` is set, it wins and `stack` is kept
as sent. Either way the frames are then mapped through the source maps
uploaded for `release` before grouping. Scrubbed before storage.

tags.description: Typed tags, at most 64.

last_release.description:
The release of the latest occurrence. Release is an attribute of each
occurrence, never part of the group key: one bug stays one group across
releases.

name.description: `orgs/{org}/projects/{project}/envs/{env}/error_groups/{error_group}`.

title.description: The exception type and message of the first occurrence.

sylphx.observability.v1.ErrorGroupState.description: The triage state of an error group.

sylphx.observability.v1.Generation.description:
A Generation is one Sylphx AI inference call of a project environment
(Responses, Messages, Chat Completions, embeddings, images, audio), read
from the OpenTelemetry GenAI span the AI gateway emits for it
(services/ai/docs/telemetry.md). It is a view over the environment's
traces, so it has no store of its own and expires with them. It never
names how the call was served: no route, account or vendor endpoint, and
no cost other than the price the caller was charged. Prompts and outputs
are not here. The id is the span id.

api_key.description: The key that made the call, as a resource name.

api_surface.description:
The wire the call used: `responses`, `messages`, `chat_completions`,
`embeddings`, `images`, `audio` or `realtime_transcription`.

cache_read_input_tokens.description: Input tokens read from the prompt cache.

cache_write_input_tokens.description: Input tokens written to the prompt cache.

data_policy.description: The data policy the call ran under: `standard`, `zdr` or `training`.

end_time.description: When the last byte of the answer was sent.

end_user.description: The caller's own end-user id (`user` or `safety_identifier`), as sent.

error_type.description:
`error.type` when the call failed: the public error code, for example
`rate_limited`.

name.description: `orgs/{org}/projects/{project}/envs/{env}/generations/{generation}`.

price_usd.description:
What the call was charged in USD, as a decimal string, for example
`0.000420`; the same value as the response's `usage.sylphx.price`.

request_model.description:
The catalogue model id the caller named, for example
`anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5`.

response_model.description: The catalogue model id that answered.

span_id.description: The W3C span id (16 hex) of the gateway's span.

start_time.description: When the gateway received the call.

tags.description:
The caller's tags (`Sylphx-Tags` and the request's `metadata`), at most
64; filter as `tags.<key> = "value"`.

time_to_first_chunk.description: From receipt to the first output chunk; unset when nothing streamed.

trace_id.description: The W3C trace id (32 hex); the caller's own when it sent `traceparent`.

sylphx.observability.v1.GenerationOutcom.description: GenerationOutcome is how a Generation ended.

sylphx.observability.v1.LogEntry.description:
A Log Entry is one typed, bounded log record of a project environment,
correlated to a trace. Entries are immutable; ingest is idempotent per
batch.

name.description: `orgs/{org}/projects/{project}/envs/{env}/log_entries/{log_entry}`.

filter.description: AIP-160 filter over the typed, allowlisted fields.

page_size.description: At most this many; default 100, clamped to 1000.

page_token.description:
`next_page_token` of the previous page; bound to tenant, interval, filter,
and order.

parent.description: The parent the method acts in.

start_time.description: The interval start; required, at most 31 days before `end_time`.

next_page_token.description: The token of the next page; empty on the last page.

`next_page_token` of the previous page; bound to tenant, interval, filter,
and order.

next_page_token.description: The token of the next page; empty on the last page.

sylphx.observability.v1.ScrubbingPolicy.description:
The Scrubbing Policy of a project environment: what is removed from every
captured error before it is stored. The default rules always apply: fields
named like a password, secret, token, key, cookie, session, authorization,
or card are replaced with `[Filtered]`, and card numbers, bearer tokens,
JWTs, and Sylphx secret keys are replaced wherever they appear. Email
addresses are replaced unless `keep_emails` is set. The environment's
policy adds to the defaults; it cannot remove them.

denied_fields.description:
More field names to replace with `[Filtered]` wherever they appear in
tags, extra data, request data, or breadcrumb data (case-insensitive,
matched as a substring), at most 64.

keep_emails.description: Keep email addresses instead of replacing them with `[email]`.

name.description: `orgs/{org}/projects/{project}/envs/{env}/scrubbing_policies/default`.

sylphx.observability.v1.SourceMap.description:
A Source Map is one uploaded JavaScript source map of one release of a
project environment. Captured stack frames of that release whose file
matches `file_url` are mapped back to the original source before grouping.
Uploading the same release and file again replaces the map.

content.description:
The source map JSON (revision 3), at most 16 MiB. Written, never read
back.

file_url.description:
The minified file the map describes: its URL
(`https://app.example.com/assets/index-3f2a.js`) or its path
(`/assets/index-3f2a.js`). A frame matches on the URL path.

name.description: `orgs/{org}/projects/{project}/envs/{env}/source_maps/{source_map}`.

release.description: The release the map belongs to, as sent in `ErrorEvent.release`.

uid.description: `smp_<digest>`; the same release and file always have the same id.

end_time.description: When the span ended; not before `start_time`.

parent_span_id.description: The parent span id; empty for a root span.

app_frame.description: Whether the frame is the customer's own code.

sylphx.observability.v1.Trace.description:
A Trace is every span sharing one W3C trace id in a project environment. The
id is `t` followed by the 32-hex trace id.

has_error.description: Whether any span has an error status.

name.description: `orgs/{org}/projects/{project}/envs/{env}/traces/{trace}`.

spans.description: Every span, in start order; empty in query results.

scrubbing_policy.description: The scrubbing policy to update; `name` identifies it.

update_mask.description: The fields to write; unset writes every populated field.

log_entries.description: The entries, at most 1000; only record fields are read.

parent.description: The parent the method acts in.
The parent the method acts in.

channel.description: The channel its events are published to, `namespace:name`.

sylphx.realtime.v1.Capability.description: Capability is one thing a token lets its holder do on a channel pattern.

sylphx.realtime.v1.ChannelGrant.description: ChannelGrant is the capabilities a token grants on one channel pattern.

capabilities.description: The capabilities granted. At least one.

pattern.description:
A channel name or pattern: `room:42`, or `room:*` for every channel of the
namespace. `*` is allowed only as the whole name part, and never in the
namespace part.

name.description: The namespace name.
The namespace name.

sylphx.realtime.v1.HistoryPreset.description:
HistoryPreset is how much of a channel's past a namespace keeps. Longer
retention is not a realtime feature: route the channel's messages to an
Events topic.

grants.description:
The channels and capabilities to grant. A channel token takes exactly one
grant whose pattern has no `*`. At most 64 grants.

kind.description: Which kind of token to mint.

ttl.description: How long the token lives; 1 minute to 24 hours, default 1 hour.

user.description: The end user's id. Required for a connection token.

claims.description: The claims the service put in it, for the caller to log or check.

connect_uri.description:
The realtime host the client connects to. Never hard-code it: it can
change, with no port, and the protocol-v1 paths are fixed.

expire_time.description: When it expires.

refresh_time.description:
The earliest the client should ask for a replacement: the in-band
`refresh_required` frame arrives at this time.

token.description:
The token. Opaque; sent in the `connect` frame or the `Authorization`
header, never in a URL.

cursor.description:
Return messages after this cursor. Empty starts at the oldest kept
message.

page_size.description: At most this many messages; default 100, at most 1,000.

wait_seconds.description:
When no message is after the cursor, wait up to this many seconds for
one; 0 to 30, default 0 (answer at once).

messages.description: The messages, oldest first. Empty when the wait ran out.

next_cursor.description:
The cursor to pass as `cursor` next. Always set unless the
namespace is ephemeral.

page_size.description: At most this many namespaces; the service caps it.

next_page_token.description: Empty on the last page.

page_size.description: At most this many members; default 100, at most 1,000.

next_page_token.description: Empty on the last page.

sylphx.realtime.v1.Member.description: Member is one connection present on a channel.

connection_id.description: The connection id, unique while the connection lives.

data.description: The application's presence data, at most 4 KiB encoded.

user.description: The user id from the token.

sylphx.realtime.v1.Message.description: Message is one message of a channel.

cursor.description:
The message's cursor: opaque, ordered within the channel, and the value
to resume from. Empty in an ephemeral namespace.

data.description: The JSON payload, at most 64 KiB encoded.

event.description: The application's event name, for example `move`. 1 to 64 characters.

publish_time.description: When the service accepted the message.

publisher.description: The user id of the publisher; empty when a server published without one.

sylphx.realtime.v1.Namespace.description:
Namespace is the only configured object of Sylphx Realtime. It carries the
rules of every channel named `<namespace>:<name>`. Channels are implicit:
they exist from their first publish or subscribe and are never created.
Declared in `sylphx.toml` as `[realtime.namespaces.<name>]`.

client_publish.description:
Whether a client holding a token with the publish capability may publish.
Default off: only servers publish.

history.description: How much history channels keep. Default NONE.

name.description:
The namespace name: 1 to 32 characters of `a-z`, `0-9`, `-` and `_`,
starting with a letter. It is the part of a channel before the first
colon, and never changes.

presence.description: Whether channels track who is present. Default off.

channel.description:
The channel, `namespace:name`: the name is 1 to 128 characters of
`a-z A-Z 0-9 - _ . =` and no `*`.

data.description: The JSON payload, at most 64 KiB encoded.

event.description: The application's event name, 1 to 64 characters.

message.description: The published message; its cursor is empty in an ephemeral namespace.

name.description: The namespace name; see Namespace.name.

sylphx.realtime.v1.TokenClaims.description:
TokenClaims are the claims every Sylphx Realtime token carries. A token is
opaque to SDK users; this message states what the service puts in it and
what it checks.

cell.description: The authoritative Access cell id of the issuing tenant. Required.

environment.description:
The authoritative Access environment id, not a client-supplied value.
Valid only within the organization, project and cell below.

expire_time.description:
When the token expires. Between issue time plus 1 minute and 24 hours.
The service closes a connection whose token has expired and was not
refreshed.

grants.description:
The channels the holder may use. A connection token holds the grants of
every channel its connection may touch; a channel token holds exactly one.

issuer_key_id.description:
The issuing Access key id (not its secret). Required: the service rechecks
its freshness, expiry, revocation and token-issuing authority through the
Access verifier at admission, refresh and while the connection is open.

organization.description: The authoritative Access organization id of the issuing tenant. Required.

project.description: The authoritative Access project id of the issuing tenant. Required.

token_id.description: A unique id; the service can revoke a token by it until it expires.

user.description:
The end user's id (`sub`). Required for a connection token; it is the
user shown in presence.

sylphx.realtime.v1.TokenKind.description: TokenKind says what a token connects.

release.description: The release to create; only spec and caller-writable metadata are read.

release_id.description:
The id of the new release, `^[a-z]([a-z0-9_-]{0,61}[a-z0-9])?$`; the server assigns one when
empty.

validate_only.description: Validate and return the result without writing anything.

The name of the rollout to get.

filter.description: AIP-160 filter over labels and filterable fields.

page_size.description: At most this many; default 50, clamped to 1000.

next_page_token.description: The token of the next page; empty on the last page.

filter.description: AIP-160 filter over labels and filterable fields.

page_size.description: At most this many; default 50, clamped to 1000.

next_page_token.description: The token of the next page; empty on the last page.

sylphx.release.v1.Placement.description:
Placement is attribute matching against the Cell registry: a workload is
placed on a Ready Cell that has every attribute, or refused.

cells.description: Specific cells, for example `fs01`; empty means any matching cell.

regions.description: Regions allowed, for example `fsn1`; empty means any.

sylphx.release.v1.Release.description:
A Release is an immutable desired state of an environment's workloads.
Writing a newer Release supersedes the live one; a rollback is a new
Release naming older digests.

name.description: `orgs/{org}/projects/{project}/envs/{env}/releases/{release}`.

sylphx.release.v1.ReleaseMember.description: ReleaseMember is one workload of a Release.

artifact.description: The Artifact to run, by digest.

config.description:
Plain configuration values delivered as environment variables. Never a
secret value: those are Secret bindings.

secrets.description: The Secret bindings the workload receives, each pinned to a version.

workload.description:
The workload's name in the environment, for example `api`: the owning
service's Resource id (a Hosting service, a Workflows worker, ...).

cell_count.description: How many cells the member is placed on.

converged_cell_count.description: How many cells run the member at this Release.

observed_digest.description: The digest the cells report running.

sylphx.release.v1.ReleaseSpec.description:
ReleaseSpec is the caller-writable state of a Release; it never changes
after Create.

members.description:
The workloads, each by artifact digest. A member that names a tag or an
unverified Artifact is refused.

sylphx.release.v1.ReleaseState.description: ReleaseState is the lifecycle state of a Release.

sylphx.release.v1.ReleaseStatus.description:
ReleaseStatus is the observed state of a Release, derived from Cell
Status.

live_time.description: When every cell first served the Release.

observed_generation.description: The generation this status was computed from.

previous_release.description: The Release that was live when this one was admitted.

successor.description: The Release that replaced this one.

sylphx.release.v1.Rollout.description:
A Rollout is the progress of one Release through its waves, derived from
the cell status the Release controller reports.

current_wave.description: The index of the wave in progress, from 0.

halt_reason.description: A customer-safe reason the rollout halted.

name.description: `orgs/{org}/projects/{project}/envs/{env}/rollouts/{rollout}`.

sylphx.release.v1.RolloutPolicy.description: RolloutPolicy is how a Release moves through waves.

bake_duration.description:
How long each wave bakes, healthy, before the next starts; default
10 minutes.

halt_on_failure.description: Halt the rollout when a wave's health gate fails; default true.

skip_waves.description:
Skip the waves and apply to every cell together: break-glass only, and
refused for any other principal.

sylphx.release.v1.RolloutState.description: RolloutState is the lifecycle state of a Rollout or one of its waves.

sylphx.release.v1.SecretPin.description: SecretPin pins a Secret binding to one version for a Release.

version.description:
The version it delivers; unset pins the binding's resolved version at
admission.

sylphx.release.v1.Wave.description: Wave is one step of a rollout.

end_time.description: When the wave passed its health gate or failed.

healthy_cell_count.description: How many of the wave's cells report the Release converged and healthy.

sylphx.release.v1.WaveScope.description: WaveScope is what one wave of a rollout covers.

scale_set.description: The scale set to create; only spec and caller-writable metadata are read.

scale_set_id.description: The id segment of the name; the server assigns one when unset.

sylphx.sandboxes.v1.KeyAction.description:
KeyAction presses a key combination, xdotool syntax: `Return`, `ctrl+c`,
`ctrl+shift+t`, `super`, `F5`. On Android, `home`, `back`, `app_switch`,
`power`, `volume_up`, `volume_down`, `enter`, or `KEYCODE_*`.

repeat.description: Press it this many times; default 1.

sylphx.sandboxes.v1.Lease.description:
A Lease is one isolated machine of a shape, region, and image for a bounded
time. It is granted immediately from a warm or cold machine, or refused with
a typed reason; its end destroys the machine. Sandboxes is its only writer.
Put the caller's own correlation (agent id, work id) in `meta.labels`; List
filters on them.

name.description: `orgs/{org}/projects/{project}/envs/{env}/leases/{lease}`.

sylphx.sandboxes.v1.LeaseBudget.description:
LeaseBudget bounds what one lease may consume. Reaching a bound ends the
lease with the matching EndReason; the Cell enforces it without the
control plane.

max_cost_micros.description:
End COST_BUDGET once the shape's list price times wall seconds reaches
this many millionths of a US dollar.

max_cpu_seconds.description: End CPU_BUDGET after this many vCPU-seconds of guest CPU time.

sylphx.sandboxes.v1.LeaseEndpoints.description:
LeaseEndpoints are a lease's data-plane addresses. Each accepts an Access
key with `sandboxes:exec` or a lease token of the matching scope.

cdp_uri.description: The Chrome DevTools Protocol WebSocket of a BROWSER lease.

e2b_sandbox_id.description: The E2B sandbox id this lease answers to on the E2B-compatible API.

guest_uri.description:
The guest daemon: the E2B envd protocol (Connect-RPC `process.Process`,
`filesystem.Filesystem`, HTTP `/files`), routed by the `E2b-Sandbox-Id`
header, for streaming exec and PTYs.

sylphx.sandboxes.v1.LeaseEvent.description:
A LeaseEvent is one immutable fact in a lease's life: grant, ready, end,
control changes, network changes. Events are listed in order and
long-polled with `wait`.

control.description: For CONTROL_* events: the control after the event.

control_duration.description: For CONTROL_RELEASED and CONTROL_EXPIRED: how long control was held.

lease_generation.description: The lease generation after the event.

name.description: `orgs/{org}/projects/{project}/envs/{env}/leases/{lease}/lease_events/{lease_event}`.

principal.description: The principal that caused it, when a caller did.

sequence.description: The position in the lease's event sequence, from 1.

state.description: The lease state after the event.

sylphx.sandboxes.v1.LeaseEventKind.description: LeaseEventKind is what a LeaseEvent records.

sylphx.sandboxes.v1.LeaseKind.description: LeaseKind is what a lease's machine serves.

sylphx.sandboxes.v1.LeaseNetwork.description:
LeaseNetwork is a lease's outbound policy. Link-local and cloud metadata
addresses (169.254.0.0/16, fd00:ec2::254), RFC 1918, CGNAT
(100.64.0.0/10), loopback, and the Cell's internal address ranges
are blocked under every policy and cannot be allowlisted.

allowed_cidrs.description: Public CIDRs reachable when `egress` is ALLOWLIST.

allowed_domains.description:
Hosts reachable when `egress` is ALLOWLIST: exact names or one leading
`*.` wildcard label, for example `api.openai.com`, `*.github.com`.

blocked_cidrs.description: The ranges blocked under every policy.

sylphx.sandboxes.v1.LeasePort.description: LeasePort is a guest port reachable through the lease's data plane.

visibility.description:
Default PRIVATE: a lease token or an Access key with `sandboxes:exec` is
required.

sylphx.sandboxes.v1.LeaseRefusal.description:
LeaseRefusal is the typed reason a lease was not granted. There is no global
queue: a lease is granted now or refused.

sylphx.sandboxes.v1.LeaseSpec.description: LeaseSpec is the caller-writable state of a Lease.

browser.description: The browser of a BROWSER lease.

device.description:
The device of an ANDROID lease: model and OS version
(device-farm.md §2.1). The device sets the display; `display` is
ignored.

display.description: The display of a DESKTOP, BROWSER, or ANDROID lease.

env.description:
Plain environment variables. Secrets bind through Sylphx Secrets, never
here.

idle_timeout.description:
End the lease IDLE after no data-plane call, stream input, or exec for
this long; unset never idles out.

image.description:
The image: an artifact in Sylphx Artifacts, by digest, or `template:<name>`
(`base`,
`desktop`, `browser`, `android`). Ignored when `source_snapshot` is set.

kind.description: What the machine serves; default GENERAL.

network.description: The outbound policy. Change it on a running lease with `:setNetwork`.

pool.description:
The Pool to take a warm machine from; default the platform pool for the
shape and image.

region.description: The region; default the project's home region.

source_snapshot.description: Boot from this Snapshot's disk and image instead of `image`.

ttl.description:
The maximum wall time from grant: 1 minute to 24 hours for microVMs, 24
hours to 30 days for macOS. `:renew` extends it within the shape's bound.
Reaching it ends the lease EXPIRED.

volumes.description:
Volumes attached at grant, each by name. A volume is attached to at most
one lease at a time; a volume already attached refuses the lease with
RESOURCE_IN_USE.

webhook.description:
Where lease events are delivered as signed webhooks, in addition to
`leases/*/events`.

sylphx.sandboxes.v1.LeaseState.description: LeaseState is the lease state machine (sandboxes-e2b.md §5.4).

sylphx.sandboxes.v1.LeaseStatus.description: LeaseStatus is the observed state of a Lease.

control.description: Who holds input control of the display.

display.description: The effective display, for kinds that have one.

end_reason.description: Why the lease ended, once `state` is ENDING or ENDED.

expire_time.description: When the lease ends unless renewed.

lease_generation.description:

command carries it, and a stale one is refused STALE_GENERATION.

refusal.description: Why the lease was refused, when `state` is REFUSED.

short_id.description: Eight Crockford base32 characters naming the lease in data-plane routes.

usage.description: What the lease has consumed so far.

sylphx.sandboxes.v1.LeaseUsage.description:
LeaseUsage is what a lease has consumed, refreshed at least every 60
seconds while it runs and final once it ends.

cost_micros.description:
List-price cost so far, in millionths of a US dollar; 0 on classes that
are not priced.

memory_gib_seconds.description: Memory GiB-seconds (shape memory times wall seconds).

stream_seconds.description: Seconds of live stream viewing, summed over viewers.

sylphx.sandboxes.v1.Shape.description:
A Shape is one entry of the platform's machine catalog: OS, size, the cell
capability it needs, and its lease bounds. The catalog is read-only; adding
a shape is a Release of the catalog.

The list price of one second of this shape, in millionths of a US
dollar; 0 for a class that is not priced. `spec.budget.max_cost_micros` is

viewer_uri.description:

load; the token rides in the URL fragment and never reaches a server log.

sylphx.sandboxes.v1.Volume.description:
A Volume is a persistent disk scoped to one environment, encrypted at rest
unless its class is `local`, attached by name when a lease is created. It has one writer: the lease it is
attached to, fenced by that lease's generation. It survives the lease's end
and is destroyed only by Delete.

name.description: `orgs/{org}/projects/{project}/envs/{env}/volumes/{volume}`.

sylphx.sandboxes.v1.VolumeMount.description: VolumeMount attaches a Volume to a lease.

mount_path.description: The absolute guest path; default `/home/user/volumes/{volume id}`.

sylphx.sandboxes.v1.VolumeSpec.description: VolumeSpec is the caller-writable state of a Volume.

region.description:
The region whose Cell holds the volume; default the project's home
region. A lease mounts the volume only in the same region.

size_gib.description:
Size in GiB, 1 to 1024; it may grow and never shrink. A `local` volume
never grows.

storage_class.description:
The storage class; unset means `standard`.
`standard`: replicated network storage, encrypted at rest with its own
key, attachable on any node.
`local`: fast node-local storage, not replicated, for warm build
workspaces. The guest gets it as an ext4 filesystem it formats on first
use. It pins every lease that attaches it to its node, is not encrypted at
rest, cannot grow, cannot be mounted read-only, and is lost with its node:

and storage per site, or a computer's application sign-ins. It is
secret-like: every version is envelope-encrypted under a data key of its

sylphx.workflows.v1.DistributedJob.description:
A DistributedJob runs one container image on many workers at once
(run-distributed-jobs.md §4). A run splits its work into shards that
workers lease from a queue; the worker pool grows and shrinks with the
capacity Kueue admits, and a preempted shard goes back to the queue.

A Job runs a container to completion: the project's image, a command, an
exit status, logs, and metered usage (docs/services/workflows/jobs.md). It

A Run is one execution of a Workflow, read from the engine. Create starts
it: the same `Idempotency-Key` and input return the same Run, a changed
input under the same key is refused. A Run ends `succeeded` only from its handler's recorded
result, and `cancelled` only from an authenticated cancel the handler
acknowledged or a Run that never started.

`start_delay`; at most 365 days ahead. A Run cancelled before then closes
`cancelled` with no invocation.

start_delay.description: Delay the first invocation by this much.

workflow_generation.description: The Workflow generation the Run pinned at start.

code.description:
A machine-readable code, for example `handler_rejected` or
`card_declined`.

fire is an engine timer; `(schedule, intended time)` is the Run identity, so
one instant starts at most one Run.
A fire is not a Run result.

One unit of a DistributedRun's work, leased by one worker at a time. A
lease that stops heartbeating returns the shard without counting an
attempt. Shards are read as a paged view of their run (`:readShards`).

completion.description: The pinned tool call used by the runtime to deliver the terminal result.

credentials.description: Captured credential bindings by alias; credentials never enter context.

environment.description:
Optional overrides of the environment in the pinned AgentVersion's frozen
spec, never the Agent's current head. Omitted or empty with no mask keeps
that default unchanged. Only selected fields are overlaid; see
environment_mask. The effective environment must have a supported shape,
finite positive TTL and valid repository, network and budget before admission.

environment_mask.description:
Fields of environment to overlay, relative to EnvironmentSpec, using proto
snake_case paths such as ttl, repo.uri, repo.revision,
egress.allowed_domains and budget.max_cost_micros. The wire value is a
comma-separated string; SDK property naming does not change these paths.
Omitted or empty infers populated serialized leaf fields recursively,
preserving unselected siblings from the pinned version. Proto defaults
(including empty lists) need an explicit mask to reset a selected field.
Selected lists replace, rather than append to, the inherited list.
The sole path "*" replaces the whole environment, resetting unpopulated
fields. Unknown, invalid and output-only paths are rejected, as is a
nonempty mask without environment. Effective validation also applies to
explicit resets and whole-environment replacement.

Moves a federated or device identity from one end user to another, to
fix a wrongly linked player. One transaction: the identity changes owner,
the sessions of both end users are revoked, and nothing else about
either moves (profile, memberships, data). Refused when it would leave
the source with no sign-in, unless the source is suspended, and when the
target already has an identity of the same provider. The reason is
audited with the operator, both end users and the identity's fingerprint.
An operator action: an end user's own session cannot call it.

post.description:
Verifies a store purchase for an app with no server: called with the
environment's publishable key (`billing:client`), the subject is an
install id (`inst_` and a UUID), and Money completes the purchase with the
store (acknowledges or consumes it) so the app never calls the store's
server API. Works only on store connections that set `client_verify`.
Re-calling returns the same record and grant.

account_token.description:
The account token the app set at purchase (Play `obfuscatedAccountId`,
App Store `appAccountToken`). A consistency check only: it must match
the subject's derivation and the store's copy.

package_name.description: Google Play: the package name, when the connection covers several.

product_id.description: Google Play: the store product id (for a subscription, its id).

signed_transaction.description: App Store: the StoreKit 2 signed transaction (`jwsRepresentation`).

subject.description: Who bought it: `end_user` of `inst_` and a lower-case UUID.

post.summary: Verifies a store purchase for an app with no server: called with the environment's publishable key (`billing:client`), the subject is an install id (`inst_` and a UUID), and Money completes the purchase with the store (acknowledges or consumes it) so the app never calls the store's server API. Works only on store connections that set `client_verify`. Re-calling returns the same record and grant.

post.description:
Verifies a store purchase with the store, binds it to the subject, and
returns its record and a signed grant. Re-verifying returns the same
record and grant. Called from the app's server with a secret key that
holds `billing:write`; a publishable key cannot call it.

bundle_id.description: App Store, with `transaction_id`: the app's bundle id.

package_name.description: Google Play: the package name, when the connection covers several.

product_id.description: Google Play: the store product id (for a subscription, its id).

signed_transaction.description: App Store: the StoreKit 2 signed transaction (`jwsRepresentation`).

transaction_id.description:
App Store, instead of `signed_transaction`: the transaction id, for apps
on original StoreKit whose receipts carry no signed transaction. Money
reads the transaction from Apple with the connection's key; Apple's
signed answer is the proof.

validate_only.description:
Verify fully and return the verdict Money would give, without writing
anything: no record, no subject binding, no Google Play acknowledge or
consume, no entitlement, no ledger posting, no event, and no signed
`grant_token`. Refusals are exactly the ones a real call gives. For
moving existing store sales onto Money, by comparing verdicts with the
seller's own path before switching.

post.summary: Verifies a store purchase with the store, binds it to the subject, and returns its record and a signed grant. Re-verifying returns the same record and grant. Called from the app's server with a secret key that holds `billing:write`; a publishable key cannot call it.

Searches an index by text, by vector, or both, best match first, with
filters and paging.

filters.description: Conditions every hit meets, at most 16.

limit.description: At most this many hits, 1 to 100; unset is 20.

offset.description: Hits to skip; offset + limit is at most 1000.

prefix.description:
Whether the query's last word also matches as a word prefix; unset is
true.

query.description:
Text to match, in web-search syntax: words (all must match), "quoted
phrases", `or`, and `-word` to exclude. The last word also matches as a
word prefix unless `prefix` is false.

vector.description:
An embedding to match by cosine similarity; its length is the index's
vector dimensions.

vector_weight.description: The vector list's share of a hybrid score, 0 to 1; unset is 0.5.

post.summary: Searches an index by text, by vector, or both, best match first, with filters and paging.

tags.description:
Sylphx Access (preview). AccessService is Sylphx Access: orgs, projects, environments, and API keys.
Access is the only writer of these types.
tags.name: access

tags.description:
Sylphx Agents (preview). AgentsService is Sylphx Agents, the platform's hosted agent runtime
(ADR-01M495TCCBZGSQ68A4P4G428H2). Apps call it instead of building their
own agent loop, session store, memory and credential handling.

Scopes: `agents:read` and `agents:write` manage agents, versions and
memory stores with a secret key. `agents:sessions` runs sessions and reads
and deletes session and memory records. All methods currently require a
secret key. Publishable-key access is deferred until the backend enforces
end-user ownership of sessions and memories and `end_user_access` on Agents.
Credential actions capture existing grants; handles are not CRUD resources.
tags.name: agents

tags.description:
Sylphx AI (preview). AiService is the Resource side of Sylphx AI: the model catalog.

Inference is not here. The OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible routes
(`/v1/responses`, `/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/messages`, `/v1/embeddings`,
`/v1/images/*`, `/v1/audio/*`, `/v1/models`, `/v1/files`) keep their
industry wire and stay outside the Resource grammar (ai-inference-surface.md
§4, resource-api-and-clients.md §4.6); their contract is imported OpenAPI,
not proto. Usage is not here either: AI keeps no usage or spend table
(AI-USAGE-SPEND); its meters are read from Kernel Billing.
tags.name: ai

tags.description:
Sylphx Artifacts (preview). ArtifactsService is Sylphx Artifacts: immutable content by digest, with
its SBOM and provenance. Sylphx Build writes them; Release reads them.
tags.name: artifacts

tags.description:
Sylphx Generated Assets (preview). AssetsService is Sylphx Generated Assets: declare images in code, generate
them once, lock them, and serve them from a CDN by content hash. An Asset
holds a recipe and its variants; `:generate` makes what is missing, and
`:lock` returns the `assets.lock` text a build commits. Generation happens
only in these calls, never at build or run time.
tags.name: assets

tags.description:
Sylphx Auth (preview). AuthService is Sylphx Auth's management surface: sign-in for a customer's
own users, their sessions, customer organizations, and OAuth clients.
Sylphx orgs, members, principals, and keys are Sylphx Access, never Auth.
End-user ceremonies (sign-in, recovery, OAuth authorize and token) are
protocol endpoints, not Resource methods.
tags.name: auth

tags.description:
Sylphx Billing (preview). BillingService is Sylphx Billing: the meter and plan catalog, each org's
billing account and plan, its invoices, usage, and budget leases. Usage
arrives through each service's spool, never through this API; no request
path calls Billing.
tags.name: billing

tags.description:
Sylphx Broker (preview). BrokerService is the credential service: workload identity in, short-lived
scoped provider credential out.
tags.name: broker

tags.description:
Sylphx Build (preview). BuildService is Sylphx Build: one command or one image over a commit or an
uploaded tree, on an offline build lease beside a warm workspace, with one
cache per project. Images carry an SBOM and signed SLSA provenance, all
written to Sylphx Artifacts by digest.
tags.name: build

tags.description:
Sylphx Config (preview). ConfigService is Sylphx Config: dynamic configuration and feature flags
evaluated in each cell from that cell's snapshot.
tags.name: config

tags.description:
Sylphx Connections (preview). ConnectionsService is Sylphx Connections: Connection Providers and their
installations as Resources.
tags.name: connections

tags.description:
Sylphx Data (preview). DataPlaneService is the data plane of Sylphx Data: object bytes, key-value
entries (strings, counters, hashes, lists, and sorted sets), and search
documents in an environment's buckets, KV namespaces, and search indexes. It is
served by Data itself at its origin, not by the Resource API, and is called
with the environment's secret key (`SYLPHX_API_KEY`); the key's org,
project, and environment are the tenant. Every call carries a new
`Sylphx-Effect-Id`, which the SDK sends and reuses on retries.

The buckets, namespaces, and indexes themselves are Resources of
DataService. The
messages here are Data's wire format
(`services/data/proto/sylphx/data/v1/data.proto`), field for field; Data
answers ProtoJSON (camelCase names, 64-bit integers and bytes as strings).
tags.name: data

tags.description:
Sylphx Entitlement (preview). EntitlementService is the read-only view of Sylphx Entitlement. Billing
writes it through the Resource store; this service has no mutation.
tags.name: entitlement

tags.description:
Sylphx Events (preview). EventsService is Sylphx Events: the event bus, queues, outbound and inbound
webhooks, and realtime channels. Publish, lease, ack, and delivery run in
each cell from that cell's snapshot.
tags.name: events

tags.description:
Sylphx Hosting (preview). HostingService is Sylphx Hosting: Services that build from source or run an
existing Artifact, ship as Releases in waves, get a Preview per pull
request, and read their source through a SourceLink.
tags.name: hosting

tags.description:
Sylphx Keys (preview). KeysService is Sylphx Keys: non-exportable keys on the regional signer.
Callers use a key; no method returns key material.
tags.name: keys

tags.description:
Sylphx Knowledge (preview). KnowledgeService is Sylphx Knowledge: one permission-aware knowledge graph
that people, apps and agents write while they work and read through search
with citations. Episodes are the sources; entities and relations (facts)
are what is known, each with provenance and valid and recorded time.
Every record lives in one Space, and a caller sees a record only through a
space it may read, so a context pack or an answer never cites a source the
caller cannot open.
tags.name: knowledge

tags.description:
Sylphx Localization (preview). LocalizationService is Sylphx Localization: translate an app's strings in CI
with AI, a translation memory, and a glossary. A Catalog holds the source
messages and their translations; `:sync` translates what is new or changed,
and `:export` returns the files per locale with a QA report. Translation
happens only in these calls, never at build or run time.
tags.name: localization

tags.description:
Sylphx Money (preview). MoneyService is Sylphx Money's customer payments: an app sells to its own
users through the stores and processors Money integrates once, and asks one
question on its request path, "does this subject have this feature"
(docs/services/money/customer-payments.md).
tags.name: money

tags.description:
Sylphx Network (preview). NetworkService is Sylphx Network: verified domains, exact routes served by
each cell's edge from its snapshot, certificates Sylphx terminates, declared
egress addresses, and private links.
tags.name: network

tags.description:
Sylphx Notify (preview). NotifyService is Sylphx Notify: messages to people over email, SMS, push,
and in-app inbox, with preferences, suppression, templates, and broadcasts.
Notify is built on Sylphx Events as an ordinary customer.
tags.name: notify

tags.description:
Sylphx Observability (preview). ObservabilityService is Sylphx Observability's log, trace, and error
surface: ingest through the emitter-side buffer, tenant-fenced bounded
queries, and error-group triage. Observability is only ever a soft
dependency.
tags.name: observability

tags.description:
Sylphx Realtime (preview). ChannelService is the Channel API of Sylphx Realtime: the server side that
configures namespaces, publishes, reads history, lists presence, and mints
the tokens clients connect with. It is served by the Events service at the
Realtime origin, not by the Resource API, and is called with the
environment's secret key (`SYLPHX_API_KEY`); the key's org, project and
environment are the tenant. Clients connect with a token over the Sylphx
channel protocol v1 (`protocol.proto`).

The same calls become MCP tools. An agent cannot hold a socket, so
ListMessages with `wait_seconds` is its subscribe.
tags.name: realtime

tags.description:
Sylphx Release (preview). ReleaseService is Sylphx Release: the only deployable unit and the progress
of its rollouts. Releases are immutable; there is no Update or Delete.
tags.name: release

tags.description:
Sylphx Runners (preview). RunnersService is Sylphx Runners: CI runners of a class
`sylphx-<os>-<size>`, one clean Sandboxes lease per job, registered as scale
sets on a Sylphx Runners installation. Runners are read-only: GitHub matches
jobs to runners, and Runners reports them.
tags.name: runners

tags.description:
Sylphx Sandboxes (preview). SandboxesService is Sylphx Sandboxes: isolated machines leased for a bounded
time, granted immediately or refused with a typed reason, and destroyed
before anyone else can touch them.
Every agent-computer surface is here: exec and files, computer actions that
map one-to-one onto the Anthropic computer tool and OpenAI computer-use
actions and return the post-action screenshot in the same call, CDP, live
streams, and human takeover. The streaming guest protocol (E2B envd) is
served at `status.endpoints.guest_uri`.
tags.name: sandboxes

tags.description:
Sylphx Secrets (preview). SecretsService is Sylphx Secrets: write-only, versioned values and the
bindings that deliver them. Reading a value back is the separate break-glass
permission `secrets:access`.
tags.name: secrets

tags.description:
Sylphx Workflows (preview). WorkflowsService is Sylphx Workflows: durable execution, schedules, timers,
and runs. Workflows is the one writer of these types.
tags.name: workflows
